ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners ('RBE') implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849; Grand-Ducal regulations and CSSF circulars implementing the EU AML/CFT framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte notarié) including articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed authenticated by the notary; no apostille required, but deed is published in the RESA electronic legal journal and filed with the RCSL

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each shareholder and beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the passport-issuing state or recognized consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for documents from non-EU / non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from criminal record (casier judiciaire) of each proposed manager/Gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial authority of the manager's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of residence and bank reference for registered office and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority of the registered office or a licensed EU/Luxembourg bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille if issued by an EU financial institution; otherwise Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate shareholder dossier – certificate of incorporation, extract from trade register, register of directors, and memorandum/articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or competent corporate registry of the shareholder's state of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, gérants and signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council resolutions, OFAC lists (where multinational transactions exist), and Luxembourg domestic sanctions maintained by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF). All politically exposed persons (PEPs), their families and close associates must undergo enhanced due diligence under Article 3(7) and Article 5 of the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. Source of funds, source of wealth, and negative verification against LuxTrust and CSSF guidance are documented and retained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be in Latin script. The RCSL records the name in the language of the deed, which must be French, German, Luxembourgish, or another European language with a transliteration into Latin characters. The name must be sufficiently distinctive, contain no misleading terms, and comply with public order and morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCSL does not operate a formal name reservation system; availability is confirmed during the notarial filing. If the RCSL rejects the proposed name, the notary must submit a corrective amendment or file a fresh name. A formal judicial appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 30 days of the rejection notification, pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies. No extension of the 30-day window is permitted; a new name may be re-filed without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation services are permissible for the registered office of an SARL under generally applicable rules; however, for a ship crew recruitment agency (ISIC 5222) licensed as a maritime employment agency, a physical operational office staffed by management in Luxembourg is mandatory. A virtual-only office will not satisfy commercial substance requirements for the statutory licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: MODERATE_TO_HIGH (65-75% estimated probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months by the Ministry of Economy, Ministry of Labour, or the police due to crew recruitment and data protection sensitivities)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (SARL); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2011 on the Trade and Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized incorporation deed (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association, followed by RCS electronic registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must subscribe a minimum share capital of EUR 12,000. At formation, cash subscriptions must be paid up to at least 25% of the subscribed amount, with a statutory floor of EUR 3,000, deposited in a blocked bank account in Luxembourg in the name of the company in formation or held by the notary until registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up and certified. No separate escrow authority exists beyond notarial or banking control.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation deed dated [date] is ratified and the share capital subscriptions are accepted as validly made pursuant to Article 710-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the management is authorized to effect all RCS filings and publications. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] are appointed as managers and authorized signatories, acting jointly or individually as provided in the articles. RESOLVED, that bank accounts, payroll mandates, and access to the Luxembourg Business Registers be opened and administered by the appointed managers, and all necessary maritime crew recruitment and placement licensing applications are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Form Pre-Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS Name Reservation Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search and file a formal reservation for the proposed corporate name, stating the SARL legal form and the object of ship crew recruitment and placement. The request is submitted electronically through the LBR portal with the proposed articles of association attached in draft.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association in French or German
Relevant extract of the intended ISIC 5222 activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to identity or conflict with a protected mark, promptly file an amended name reservation with a distinctive secondary element, or submit a written observation to the RCS. The reservation period may be extended by written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Blocked Capital Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary's escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the company in formation, deposit at least EUR 3,000 as partial contribution to the EUR 12,000 minimum capital, and obtain a capital deposit certificate from the bank for presentation to the notary. The account remains blocked until the RCS registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Identification documents and beneficial ownership declarations for all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML objections, provide enhanced source-of-funds documentation and a reasoned beneficial ownership structure. If banking refusal persists, instruct the notary to hold escrow funds through a qualified intermediary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the finalized draft articles, capital deposit certificate, and shareholder identity files to the notary. The notary reviews legal compliance, checks restrictions on SARL managers, and prepares the notarial deed and appendices for execution.
required_dossiers: Identities and residential addresses of shareholders and managers
Statement of contribution type (cash and/or in-kind)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query on capital contribution, governance clause, or permitted object, amend the draft articles and resubmit. Any in-kind contribution must be supported by an auditor's report when required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarized Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders or their duly authorized notarial proxies and the first managers appear before the notary. The notary reads the final deed, confirms payments, receives signatures, and converts the deed into authentic form as the official incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national identity cards
If proxies: notarized powers of attorney
Declaration of no criminal disqualification for managers, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Absence of a shareholder or manager is cured by a Luxembourg-compliant notarial proxy. If the notary identifies defective signatures or missing annexes, the signing session is adjourned and the corrected deed is re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the eJustice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the authenticated copy of the incorporation deed electronically with the RCS. The RCS examines the file, assigns a corporate registration number, and publishes the incorporation extract in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), completing the company's legal existence as of the RCS registration date.
required_dossiers: RCS filing forms signed by managers
Identification and signatures of authorized managers
Statement that the registered office is in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a query or rejects registration, the notary and managers submit a rectification or additional legal justification via the eJustice portal. Minor omissions are cured by filing supplementary declarations, and the registration date is preserved if corrected within the statutory time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Social and Tax Visibility Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for social security as an employer, obtain the matriculation number from CCSS, and register for VAT, corporate income tax and municipal business tax with the AEDT. The applicant declares the intended activity of ship crew recruitment and payroll services.
required_dossiers: Activity declaration for VAT and direct tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or social security office requests clarifications on the payroll operating model or place of supply, submit a written explanation of the crew management fee structure and employer versus payroll agent roles. Errors are corrected by amending the registration forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works – Administration of Maritime Affairs and Navigation (Administration de la navigation – service maritime); consultation with the Ministry of Labour for private placement of seafarers
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Maritime Crew Recruitment and Placement Agency Licence (Licence d'agence privée de recrutement et de placement des gens de mer)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental registration only – Category RC (activities not requiring a full EIA report); the office-based crew recruitment and payroll agency does not trigger a full environmental impact assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater; office sanitary effluents must comply with municipal sewerage regulations. No VOCs or combustion emissions are anticipated. Waste handling must comply with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and any applicable corporate waste collection contracts. Fleet/casualty operations, if any, remain subject to maritime environmental rules of the flag state and the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Grand Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office, including a structural load inspection for office occupancy and an evacuation plan. Occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming workplace safety, first-aid equipment, electrical installation conformity, and compliance with Luxembourg labour law for office workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg Registration, Estates, and VAT Authority; online portals: MyGuichet.lu and aedt.public.lu for VAT registrations and tax filings. Direct corporate income tax registration remains with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or newly incorporated SARL must first be registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the national identification number ('matricule d'identification') issued by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). VAT registration is then made separately with the AEDT via Form 246 for non-established taxable persons or through the MyGuichet.lu portal for established entities. Supporting documents typically include: certificate of incorporation, excerpts from the RCS, articles of association, postal address in Luxembourg or a local tax representative, bank account details, and a signed declaration of intended activity. The AEDT assigns a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU-trademarkamadeup) upon successful submission; approval generally takes 1 to 3 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – The SARL is a fully taxable Luxembourg-resident company subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on a worldwide income basis, with credit/relief for permanent establishments abroad. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Luxembourg domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a 'check-the-box' election regime. Available formal elections include: VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) for fiscal unity; election to form a qualifying joint venture and tax consolidation regime for a 95%-owned group (Tax-consolidated group filing); election for the 80% participation exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive to avoid withholding tax; and elections for the enhanced intellectual-property box regime. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 1 and 2 are mandatory and do not permit elective opt-outs except as prescribed for dividends and controlled foreign company income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For an established Luxembourg taxable person, the annual turnover exemption threshold is EUR 35,000 under the small-business franchise scheme. For non-established foreign entities, there is no threshold: any supply of goods or services physically performed or deemed supplied in Luxembourg triggers a mandatory VAT registration from the first euro unless the place of supply is outside Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates electronic invoicing for business-to-government (B2G) invoices through PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 since 1 April 2022, processed via the Luxembourg interoperability platform under the L.2020 law. For B2B transactions, e-invoicing remains optional and there is no real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous-transaction-control (CTC) reporting, and no XML/digital stamping regime in force as of the current Luxembourg VAT law. Taxpayers must however retain digital invoice audit files to satisfy AEDT inspection requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to intra-Community and third-country exports of goods where the goods physically leave the EU and the exporter retains transport evidence. For maritime crew recruitment services, VAT is zero-rated under Article 148 of the EU VAT Directive when such services are supplied for direct needs of a qualifying sea-going vessel used for international navigation, or when the supplied crew services are placed at the disposal of a non-EU ship-operator for commercial voyages. For purely B2B services to a non-EU taxable person outside of those maritime exceptions, the place of supply is outside Luxembourg and no Luxembourg VAT is charged, though this is not formally an export zero-rating. The taxpayer must document the non-EU status of the recipient (VAT/GST identification or equivalent), the nature of the vessel and its qualifying international use, and the commercial reality of the overseas delivery of services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD customs declaration in destination territory) or Intrastat dispatch records for intra-EU movements
Bill of Lading, sea-waybill, or air waybill evidencing actual transport to a third-country destination
Commercial invoice and intercompany/service agreement describing the exact crew recruitment service supplied
Packing list and transport insurance certificate (for goods) evidence of departure from Luxembourg territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation showing settlement received from the non-EU counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts substantive audit review of zero-rated export claims, examining the movement of goods or the place of service in conjunction with the transport documentation, the vessel's registration and voyage records, and the payment trail. A fraudulent or unsubstantiated zero-rating claim is subject to, without limitation: immediate VAT reassessment at 17% plus default interest (legal interest plus 4% per month for late payment), a 10% increase in the VAT due where negligence is proven, administrative fines up to EUR 100,000 for deliberate violation, and criminal penalties of up to 5 years' imprisonment for tax fraud under Luxembourg's revised General Tax Law. A retrospective clawback may reach back to the date of the original claim and triggers a refund not being allowed until the corrected assessment is issued.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the national authority licensing banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions; the European Central Bank (ECB) holds ultimate monetary and capital-movement policy competence for the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital; no exchange control approval, no prior administrative authorization, and no capital-export restrictions apply to profit remittance, dividend distributions, or inbound equity subscriptions. Practical hurdles are limited to (i) mandatory BCL balance-of-payments (BoP) statistical reporting for resident entities executing cross-border settlements of EUR 12,500 or more, (ii) binding EU/UN sanctions and targeted restrictive measures, and (iii) the statutory Luxembourg 15% dividend withholding tax (reducible under applicable tax treaties). No sector-specific restriction exists for maritime crew recruitment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg and the euro area impose no export-proceeds surrender requirement. There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for crew-agency service fees, manning fees, or disbursement reimbursement received from shipowners. Such receipts may be held in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency in offshore or onshore accounts without central-bank conversion or repatriation; they must only be reported for BCL statistical/BoP purposes and matched to the underlying manning agreements for transfer-pricing and substance documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for ancillary multi-currency crew-payroll disbursement, but not for principal corporate treasury functions. CSSF-licensed or EU-passported electronic-money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 can provide faster low-value cross-border payment rails, FX conversion, and seafarer payroll cards, subject to client-fund safeguarding rules and the EU Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU 2015/847). Legal constraints: an EMI cannot hold the notarized capital escrow, cannot grant credit, may only deploy payment accounts rather than current accounts, and must be passported within the EEA; therefore the SARL must retain a full-service Luxembourg credit institution as its primary banking counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one natural-person director or authorized signatory is the prevailing Luxembourg market practice, although not an absolute statutory requirement. CSSF-compliant remote onboarding can be achieved through video-identification and qualified electronic signatures (eIDAS), but banks customarily demand either an in-person interview at the branch, a notarized signature specimen, apostilled certified corporate documents, and certified passports of all UBOs, or alternatively a Luxembourg-based legal counsel holding an original notarized power of attorney. For a crew-recruitment agency with a foreign shipowner client base, an initial in-country meeting with the compliance officer is strongly advised to de-risk sector-specific questions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or unverifiable identification of ultimate beneficial owners at the Luxembourg RBE registry when the account file is opened.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated RBE registry extract, full Group ownership chart detailing share percentages, notarized share register excerpt, apostilled/legalized passports of all UBOs holding over 25%, tax-residence certificates, and a CSSF-format source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of wealth/funds for the SARL's initial capital deposit and the subsequent operational funding routed from foreign shareholders or shipowner sponsors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month prime-bank reference from the paying bank, notarized deed of capital subscription, audited source-of-wealth file (bank statements, dividend/sale documents, loan agreements), and a notarized AML/CFT declaration of the ultimate human person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits arising from cross-border crew-payment destinations, shipowner flags of convenience, or charterer counterparties in the maritime sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current EU/UN sanctions risk policy of the SARL, documented OFAC/EU sanctions-screening logs showing clear status of all seafarers/shipowners, Paris-MOU white-flag list, and verifiable IMO Seafarer (SID) identity documents for each contemplated payee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Human-trafficking or crew-abandonment industry-risk profile attributed by the bank's sector risk matrix to the crew-recruitment/crewing-agency classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006) certificate issued by a respected flag state, an ITF-approved Crew Management Agreement (CMA), audited crew payroll ledger showing no wage deduction, external seafarer-welfare auditor's certificate, and proof of contractual coverage of financial security for repatriation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of low-ticket real-time payments to foreign private individuals (seafarers) flagged by the bank's transaction-monitoring system as atypical payroll-like disbursements or potential layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MLC-compliant employment contracts and complete payroll registers matching every payment, STCW certificates of each seafarer, a GDPR-compliant crew data-processing register, outsourcing agreements signed with a regulated payroll processor, and a recurrent internal audit trail of monthly batch instructions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) foreign shareholder initiates an SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent ISO 20022) credit in EUR to the SARL's capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution; (2) the wire should carry the OECD/BCL BoP purpose classification code for direct investment in equity capital (e.g., direct-investment equity code per ECB BoP/CPC nomenclature) and a clear narrative referencing the SARL company name, the notarial deed of contribution, and the notarial file; (3) the receiving bank verifies sanctions, UBO/RBE alignment, source-of-funds, and BCL BoP reporting thresholds (EUR 12,500+ per transaction); (4) the Luxembourg notary certifies the capital as fully paid before release from escrow; and (5) the SARL records the equity injection in its statutory accounts and BCL external-position survey.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001/pain.002 ISO 20022) via EBICS for euro-denominated crew salaries paid to EEA bank accounts; (2) SWIFT MT103 for extra-EEA and non-EUR crew payments, shipowner fee remittances, and foreign supplier settlements; (3) commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT798 for structured trade settlements with shipowners and vessel operators when contractually required; (4) last-mile disbursement through CSSF-licensed EMI payroll cards or wage-transfer aggregators, always funded from the primary bank account under Transfer of Funds Regulation traceability; and (5) periodic FX conversion routed through the central bank account using pre-trade/algo FX execution lines.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (plain vanilla) on fully convertible pairs such as EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF, executed under IFEMA/ISDA documentation with a EEA-authorized credit institution or investment firm
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid seafarer-payroll currencies (CNY, INR, PHP, VND, TWD) cleared offshore and limited to economic hedging of payroll liabilities
Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for structural EUR/USD rebalancing, multi-currency crew payroll procurement, and short-term liquidity matching, subject to EMIR trade reporting and margin rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registration (Renouvellement annuel de l'immatriculation au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of the entity's initial RCS registration; filed electronically through the LBR portal with current company and manager data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: formal LBR reminder and administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; non-renewal for three consecutive months may result in administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes annuels / états financiers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year; for calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year; annual general meeting approving the accounts must be held within 6 months of the year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure to file is punishable by court-ordered fines imposed on the gérants under Art. 168 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915, public announcement of the default, and possible judicial dissolution/strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due once per calendar year in the same filing window as the RCS annual renewal; share transfers and other UBO changes must be declared within 15 days after the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance subjects the SARL and its managers to a criminal fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000, plus a court order to comply; repeated omission may trigger striking-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration fiscale - IRC / ICAP / IMW)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed with the ACD no later than 30 June of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers, or within five months of the close of a non-calendar fiscal year; extensions are available upon formal request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a late-filing penalty of 10% of the net tax due, capped at EUR 15,000, followed by an administrative default assessment and enforcement with daily interest (0.6% monthly).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (mission de révision légale) is compulsory for a SARL if on the balance-sheet date at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million; net turnover over EUR 8.8 million; average workforce over 50 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory accounts must be prepared in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP (plan comptable luxembourgeois), modeled on the EU Fourth Accounting Directive; IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be used where allowed for consolidated accounts or by listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE declaration must be kept current throughout the year; an annual confirmation of the same data is made during the LBR annual renewal cycle. Any transfer of shares altering the holding, voting rights, or control of the UBO must be filed within 15 days. Failure to file is a criminal offence; the registered agents and gérants must also approve the declaration in the LBR portal. The LBR may publish the company's default on the register if the annual confirmation is omitted.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (integrated Luxembourg City rate applicable from FY2025: 16% CIT + 6.5% municipal business tax; the 7% employment-fund solidarity surcharge was abolished as of 1 January 2025; the aggregate rate for FY2024 was 24.94%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR): 100% exemption on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% or EUR 6,000,000 held for at least 12 months in a resident or comparable non-resident company. IP Box (Art. 50bis LIR): 80% of qualifying IP-derived income is exempt, yielding an effective rate of approximately 4.5%. R&D tax credits and the investment tax credit (credit d'impôt investissement) can further reduce the effective burden. Crew placement and maritime staffing fee income from the ISIC 5222 activity remains ordinary commercial income taxable at the 22.5% integrated rate.
